name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for the week, day by day (Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner), with a shared grocery list and the family's recipe book; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, day by day
A shared grocery list grouped by aisle
The family's own recipe book, with a recipe's ingredients added to the list
Planning the week's dishes from the recipe book
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Ordering groceries from a store: a connector does that
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

settings.label: The grocery app orders go to

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Once a week, asks the agent to plan next week's meals, place the week's first order and send the family the plan with one question about what is low or out. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

routines.name: Dinner check-in
routines.description: Every afternoon, sends the family tonight's dinner and whether its fresh items are on an order. Silent when no dinner is planned or it is ordered in. The time it runs at is the time the app tells the family.

routines.name: Tomorrow's meals check-in
routines.description: Every evening, sends the family tomorrow's meals, with the dishes' videos for the cook on the days they come. Silent when nothing is planned. The time it runs at is the time the app tells the family.

routines.name: Order clock
routines.description: Every 15 minutes, hands the agent each grocery order whose time has come, to place it. No model call unless an order is due.

operations.name: guide
operations.description: The full guide for working with this app: read it before shopping, answering a job or changing meals. {}

operations.name: set_person
operations.description: Add or change one person who eats at home, found by name. { name, relationship?, group: child | adult | elder, portions?, diet?, allergies?, dislikes?, targets?, note?, remove?: true }. Keep portions, diet and the rest in the family's own words. Only the fields you send change; remove: true takes the person out of the family.

operations.name: set_house_rules
operations.description: The house's food rules; the list you send replaces the one there. { rules?: [{ kind: veg | egg | fasting | no_onion_garlic | other, days: ["Tue", "Thu"], note? }], notes?, structured?: true }. Send structured: true once a profile carried over from the old app is fully in people, rules, the cook and slots: it clears that text.

operations.name: set_cook
operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well. { name, days: ["Mon", ...], arrival: "HH:MM", makes_well?, note? }

operations.name: set_slots
operations.description: Meals beyond Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, and the meals the family orders in. { extra_slots?: [{ name, days?: ["Mon", ...], for?: [names] }], order_in?: [{ day: "Sun", slot: "Dinner", note? }] }. Each list you send replaces the one there.

operations.name: plan_week
operations.description: Plan a week of meals. { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD, mode: draft | final, meals?: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit?, keeps?: fresh | long }] }] }] }. Without meals it answers with the context to plan from (people, house, regulars, last week's dishes, the recipe book), or, when mode is final and the week is a draft, makes that draft final. With meals they become the whole week's plan, in place of what was there. A draft with meals is refused once the week has orders: change a meal with set_meal or set_dish, or send mode final with the new meals. A dish is for everyone unless you name who it is for; ingredient amounts are for this family; an ordered-in meal has no dishes. Answers { week } or { context }; a final plan also answers with orders: the week's orders, built from it (fresh items in the order covering their day, long-life ones in the first).

operations.name: set_meal
operations.description: Change one meal, found by date and slot (or meal_id) and made when it is not there. { date, slot, ordered_in?, note?, dishes?: [as in plan_week] }. Only what you send changes; dishes you send replace the meal's dishes. ordered_in: true takes its dishes away; sending dishes with it is refused, and a meal that is ordered in takes dishes only with ordered_in: false.

operations.name: set_dish
operations.description: Add, change or remove one dish. { dish_id, or meal_id, or date and slot; name?, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit?, keeps? }], position?, remove?: true }. In a meal, a dish of the same name is the one changed; otherwise it is added at the end. Only what you send changes; ingredients you send replace the dish's; position 0 is first; for: null means everyone.

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: Add or change one everyday item: what the house buys again and again whatever is cooked (milk, curd, bread, eggs). { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, keeps?: fresh | long, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. amount is what is needed each time: 1 l every day; 1 pack with every: week and times_per_week: 2; 6 pc on weekdays: ["Mon"]. Found by item and for_whom; only the fields you send change. paused_until leaves it out of the orders up to and including that date (a holiday); active: false stops it until you send active: true; remove: true deletes it. Set one only after the family confirmed it.

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on a grocery app. { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, items: [{ item, qty?, pack?, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }] }] }. Every item sent with its product_id is remembered as that item's product on the app. Answers { suggestions: [{ item, amount, unit, every: day | week, times_per_week?, orders_seen }] }: what was bought on three or more days, at least once a fortnight. It makes no everyday item itself: ask the family about each suggestion, then set_regular the ones they confirm.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it (milk); pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with. One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered.

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }; put its id on a dish with set_dish recipe_id.

operations.name: ask_low_or_out
operations.description: The week's long-life items (atta, rice, dal, oil), to ask the family about once. { week_start, low_or_out? }. Without low_or_out it answers { order_id, items, question }: send the question ("Atta, rice, toor dal: any low or out?") with the plan. When they answer, send their words (or a list of items) as low_or_out: the items they name are ordered, the rest are taken off the week's next scheduled order as things they have. An order already placed is never changed; an item that is out and on no order goes on the next one, or on a new order to place now. Answers { order }. Nothing about what is at home is kept beyond that order.

operations.name: add_to_order
operations.description: Add one item to an order. { order_id?, item, qty?, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. Without order_id it goes on the next scheduled order, or on a new order to place now when none is waiting; an order that is not scheduled is refused. item is the family's word for it; qty is the number of packs (1 when left out). Send the product the family picked (product_id and name_on_app, with its pack and price) and it is remembered as that item's product; without one the item's remembered product is used. Answers { order, line }.

operations.name: place_order
operations.description: Call just before you place a scheduled order on the grocery app. { order_id }. Answers { order, message, needs_product, needs_qty }: send message to the family first, word for word; find a product on the grocery app for each line in needs_product and set the packs of each line in needs_qty; then place the order without waiting for a yes, and record_order at once. An order that is not scheduled, or has nothing on it, is refused.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: Record what happened to an order on the grocery app. { order_id, placed?: true | false, paid?: true | false, total?, app_order_ref?, note? }. placed: true once it is placed and waiting for the person's payment; placed: false with a note when it could not be placed (it stays scheduled and is tried again). paid: true once the payment went through; paid: false when it was not paid: the order is closed as not paid and its items move to the next scheduled order (or a new one), named in rolled_into. When the answer has intro, send it to the family word for word.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Cancel an order. { order_id }. A scheduled order is cancelled. A placed order that is not yet paid is closed as not paid and its items move to the next order (rolled_into); cancel nothing on the grocery app. A paid order is refused: the person cancels it in the grocery app.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's meals, recipes, shopping list, drafts, orders, pantry stock and shopping preferences. Never keep any of it in memory or chat: read the app before you answer, change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. Read the guide operation before shopping, answering a job or changing meals. A meal is a set of recipes plus a note: when plans change, change the recipes and note (set_meal_recipes, save_meal), not just the dish text. Only you add recipes, and only after searching for the same dish under another spelling. Nothing in the app runs until it knows the household: when the family tells you who eats, their food habits, which meals to plan and where they shop, save it in their words as the household.profile setting (PATCH /a/<this app>/api/_app/settings); never fill it from guesses or the app's own rows. Background jobs (review_meal, fill_recipe, find_patterns) and background facts (shelf life, recipe lines) are your informed guesses: never ask the family about them and never message anyone for them. The app sends the reminders and menus itself; message the family only when a Shopping timeline wake asks (the price step), then ack_message; or when they talk to you. Silence means carry on. Never order without a family member's explicit yes; record it (record_yes), place the order, then record_order at once.
